subject: Community Project
title: Trip and community impact
objective_verbatim: Count/check the total with staff, deduct agreed costs if applicable, confirm the donation amount and communicate the result. Create a thank-you message/display and, where possible, arrange handover to the charity.

sow_row.student_task: Count/check the total with staff, deduct agreed costs if applicable, confirm the donation amount and communicate the result. Create a thank-you message/display and, where possible, arrange handover to the charity.
sow_row.evidence: Verified total raised/donated; thank-you email/card; impact display; charity response/receipt if available.
sow_row.skills: Numeracy; communication; community impact; financial awareness.
sow_row.adaptations: Use a prepared spreadsheet/tally; group calculation; sentence starters; visual before/after target comparison.
sow_row.exit: Did we meet our success criteria? What difference will the money make?

lesson_objective: Check a project fact, ask or share a question on the trip, and keep a sourced fact and true thank-you.
success_criteria: I can ask or share one true point.
I can show what I learned and plan a kind thank-you.

stages.adult_text: Confirm the educational link and start organising by 9 November. Complete local approval, consent, staffing, access, travel, welfare and contingency arrangements before departure. Do not treat this learning sequence as a risk assessment or booking. Use 12/18/10 active learning minutes around the actual itinerary. Keep funds with authorised adults; no pupil carries donation cash by default. If the visit cannot proceed, use the classroom source route and keep evidence truthful. Answers: share only an adult-checked total; explain a link to community contribution or impact; cite the actual observation or source.
stages.ta_brief: Confirm the educational link and start organising by 9 November. Complete local approval, consent, staffing, access, travel, welfare and contingency arrangements before departure. Stage: Today
Active learning minutes: 1
Each learner checks one source, asks or contributes one question, and records one fact with an honest thank-you. Choose speech, a question card, pointing or scribing. Record individual contribution and support; group attendance alone is not evidence of achievement.
Source: 06_SOW_EXTRACT_Cake_Sale.md, Aut2 W6, revision 2026-10-21; owner calendar instruction, revision 2026-10-25.

Year A · Lesson 11 · Week 6, w/c 7 December 2026
Stage: I DO
Active learning minutes: 3
Model the retained example: cake sales £14 plus gifts £2 gives funds £16; agreed costs £4 leaves £12. The example net target is £10. These are teaching values, never actual results. The editable chart compares the same two measures. Verify the real tally and the source for any impact claim before sharing it.
Source: 06_SOW_EXTRACT_Cake_Sale.md, Aut2 W6, revision 2026-10-21; owner calendar instruction, revision 2026-10-25.

Year A · Lesson 11 · Week 6, w/c 7 December 2026
Stage: WE DO
Active learning minutes: 4
Before the visit: hinge answer B. The float is borrowed change, not income. Check the real A–K record, agreed costs L and donation M = K − L. Retain the original target basis. Each learner checks one line. An adult confirms the amount; unresolved totals stay pending. Draft one book-first question or thank-you line before departure.
Source: 06_SOW_EXTRACT_Cake_Sale.md, Aut2 W6, revision 2026-10-21; owner calendar instruction, revision 2026-10-25.

Year A · Lesson 11 · Week 6, w/c 7 December 2026
Stage: YOU DO on the trip
Active learning minutes: 18
During the visit, use an 18-minute learning window within the locally confirmed itinerary. Allow one question, short observation and source note per learner. Questions may be spoken, read by an adult or handed over. Record the real date and source; observe one community role or act of service and link it to the project. Keep pauses and adult supervision within the visit arrangements. A charity handover happens only if separately arranged and authorised; do not imply the visit host receives the donation.
Source: 06_SOW_EXTRACT_Cake_Sale.md, Aut2 W6, revision 2026-10-21; owner calendar instruction, revision 2026-10-25.

Year A · Lesson 11 · Week 6, w/c 7 December 2026
Stage: YOU DO after the trip
Active learning minutes: 6
After the visit, use six minutes to record the personal fact and draft thanks. Keep the checked sum, source, contribution and support on L11-E1. Distinguish a thank-you to the visit host from the separate charity donation. Mark amounts planned, approved, sent or received only from real records. If the visit cannot proceed, use an adult-selected community source in the same learning window and label it classroom work.
Source: 06_SOW_EXTRACT_Cake_Sale.md, Aut2 W6, revision 2026-10-21; owner calendar instruction, revision 2026-10-25.

Use two minutes to check real activity dates, individual words, source and support. Keep approval, transfer and receipt status accurate. Adults retain responsibility for finance, consent and sharing. Retain a missing record as pending.
